def factor_range_pressure_tail_skew_attenuation(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    close = df_copy["close"]
    high = df_copy["high"]
    low = df_copy["low"]
    # primary mechanism: cycle range pressure over 60 days
    buy_pressure = (close - low).rolling(60, min_periods=20).sum()
    sell_pressure = (high - close).rolling(60, min_periods=20).sum()
    total_range = (high - low).rolling(60, min_periods=20).sum()
    range_pressure = (buy_pressure - sell_pressure) / total_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    # lightweight idea from secondary parent: tail skew as crash fragility attenuator
    ret = close.pct_change()
    skew = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=30).skew()
    neg_skew = np.clip(-skew, 0.0, 1.0)
    scale = 1.0 - 0.3 * neg_skew
    factor = range_pressure * scale
    df_copy["factor_range_pressure_tail_skew_attenuation"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_range_pressure_tail_skew_attenuation"]
description: Preserves the primary cycle range-pressure mechanism from parent g1_crossover_then_mutation_market_cycle_0002_acp_gen0_b_tail_skew_volume_as_800a1c2c, which identifies accumulation/distribution phase by close position within the trailing 60-day high-low range. Borrows the lightweight trailing return skewness idea from parent acp_gen0_b_tail_skew_volume_asymmetry: when 60-day return skew is strongly negative (left-tail crash fragility), the range-pressure signal is attenuated by a bounded factor between 0.7 and 1.0. This keeps the raw range-pressure strength most of the time, preserves cross-sectional variation, and targets improved MI/robustness without changing the core economics. Cross-sectional transform remains none to preserve raw payoff structure.
